questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: If A = 2i + 3j + k and B = i - 2j + 2k, then |A + B| equals:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: A + B = (2+1)i + (3-2)j + (1+2)k = 3i + j + 3k.
Step 2: |A + B|² = 3² + 1² + 3² = 9 + 1 + 9 = 19.
Step 3: |A + B| = √19.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The angle between vectors (i + j) and (j + k) is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: A = i + j, B = j + k.
Step 2: A·B = (0)(1) + (1)(1) + (0)(1) = 1.
Step 3: |A| = √2, |B| = √2.
Step 4: cos θ = 1/(√2 × √2) = 1/2.
Step 5: θ = 60°.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A vector of magnitude 10 is inclined at 60° to the x-axis. Its component along the x-axis is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: x-component = magnitude × cos(angle).
Step 2: = 10 × cos(60°) = 10 × 0.5 = 5.
Step 3: y-component = 10 × sin(60°) = 5√3.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Image-based: The figure shows vectors A and B placed tail-to-tail with angle θ between them. Using parallelogram method, the resultant bisects the angle when:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: In parallelogram, diagonal bisects angle only when adjacent sides are equal.
Step 2: This is a property of rhombus (parallelogram with equal sides).
Step 3: When |A| = |B|, the parallelogram is a rhombus and diagonal bisects the angle.
Step 4: This is also the condition for the angle bisector theorem to apply symmetrically.
questions.imagePrompt: Two vectors A and B with common tail O, equal lengths |A| = |B|, angle θ between them, parallelogram completed, diagonal shown bisecting angle θ into two equal angles θ/2, labeled with angle marks showing equality, clean geometric diagram

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: For what value of α are the vectors 2i - 3j + 4k and αi + 6j - 8k parallel?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Parallel vectors must be scalar multiples: (2, -3, 4) = k(α, 6, -8).
Step 2: From second components: -3 = 6k → k = -0.5.
Step 3: From third: 4 = -8k → k = -0.5. ✓
Step 4: From first: 2 = kα = -0.5α → α = -4.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A projectile is thrown with speed 20 m/s at 30° to the horizontal. Its velocity after 1 s is (g = 10 m/s²):
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Resolve initial velocity: u_x = 20cos30° = 10√3 m/s, u_y = 20sin30° = 10 m/s.
Step 2: Horizontal velocity remains constant: v_x = 10√3.
Step 3: Vertical velocity after 1 s: v_y = 10 - 10(1) = 0.
Step 4: Therefore, velocity = 10√3 i + 0 j.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The maximum range of a projectile is 100 m. The maximum height reached is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Maximum range occurs at θ = 45°: R_max = u²/g = 100.
Step 2: So u² = 100g.
Step 3: Maximum height at θ = 45°: H = u²sin²45°/(2g) = (100g)(0.5)/(2g) = 50/2 = 25 m.
Step 4: Alternatively: H = R_max/4 = 100/4 = 25 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Image-based: The velocity-time graph shows horizontal (v_x) and vertical (v_y) components for a projectile. What is the speed at the highest point?
options: Equal to vertical component at that instant
questions.explanation:
Step 1: At highest point, vertical velocity v_y = 0.
Step 2: Speed = √(v_x² + v_y²) = √(v_x² + 0) = |v_x|.
Step 3: Since v_x is constant throughout (no horizontal acceleration), speed at top equals initial horizontal component.
Step 4: This is less than initial speed (which has both components).
questions.imagePrompt: Two graphs: v_x vs t showing horizontal line at constant positive value, v_y vs t showing straight line from positive initial value decreasing through zero at t_m (marked as highest point) to negative, time axis labeled with t_m at peak, clean scientific plotting style

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A particle moves in a circle of radius 4 m with constant speed 2 m/s. The magnitude of average velocity over half revolution is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Half revolution: displacement = diameter = 8 m (from start to diametrically opposite point).
Step 2: Distance traveled = half circumference = πr = 4π m.
Step 3: Time = distance/speed = 4π/2 = 2π s.
Step 4: Average velocity = displacement/time = 8/(2π) = 4/π m/s.
Step 5: Average speed = distance/time = 4π/(2π) = 2 m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The position vector of a particle is r = (at²)i + (bt)j. The trajectory is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: x = at², y = bt.
Step 2: From y = bt, we get t = y/b.
Step 3: Substitute: x = a(y/b)² = (a/b²)y².
Step 4: This is x ∝ y², a parabola opening along x-axis.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A man can swim at 1 m/s in still water. He swims across a river 100 m wide flowing at 0.8 m/s. To reach directly opposite point, he should swim at angle θ to perpendicular where sin θ equals:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: To reach directly opposite, upstream component of swimming must cancel river flow.
Step 2: v_man × sin θ = v_river.
Step 3: 1 × sin θ = 0.8.
Step 4: sin θ = 0.8, so θ ≈ 53.13° upstream.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Image-based: The figure shows triangle law of vector addition. If |A| = 5, |B| = 12, and |A + B| = 13, the angle between A and B when placed tail-to-tail is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Using |A + B|² = |A|² + |B|² + 2|A||B|cos θ.
Step 2: 169 = 25 + 144 + 2(5)(12)cos θ = 169 + 120cos θ.
Step 3: 169 = 169 + 120cos θ → cos θ = 0.
Step 4: θ = 90°. This is a 5-12-13 right triangle.
questions.imagePrompt: Triangle with sides labeled: vector A (5 units), vector B (12 units), resultant A+B (13 units) as third side, right angle marked between A and B, Pythagorean triple 5-12-13 shown, labeled triangle diagram

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A particle in uniform circular motion has angular velocity ω. The angle between position vector and velocity vector is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Position vector r points radially outward from center.
Step 2: Velocity vector v is tangent to circle, perpendicular to radius.
Step 3: Therefore r ⊥ v, angle = 90°.
Step 4: This is fundamental property of circular motion.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question:
Passage: A projectile is launched from ground with speed 50 m/s at 37° above horizontal. (sin37° = 0.6, cos37° = 0.8, g = 10 m/s²)

Question 1: The time of flight is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: u_y = 50sin37° = 50 × 0.6 = 30 m/s.
Step 2: Time of flight T = 2u_y/g = 2 × 30/10 = 6 s.
Step 3: Time up = 3 s, time down = 3 s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Using the same projectile data, the horizontal range is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: u_x = 50cos37° = 50 × 0.8 = 40 m/s.
Step 2: Time of flight T = 6 s.
Step 3: Range R = u_x × T = 40 × 6 = 240 m.
Step 4: Alternatively: R = u²sin(2θ)/g = 2500 × sin(74°)/10 = 2500 × 0.96/10 = 240 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Image-based: The figure shows a projectile trajectory with points A, B, C at different heights. The speeds at A and C are equal when:
options: A and C are at same height
B is midway between A and C
questions.explanation:
Step 1: By energy conservation, speed depends only on height for given projectile.
Step 2: At same height, potential energy is same, so kinetic energy is same.
Step 3: Therefore speeds are equal at same height (velocities differ in direction).
Step 4: This is the symmetry property of projectile motion.
questions.imagePrompt: Parabolic trajectory with horizontal ground line, points A and C marked at same height on ascending and descending branches, point B at maximum height, velocity vectors at A (upward angle) and C (downward angle) shown with equal lengths, height lines clearly marked showing equality

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The cross product of two non-zero vectors is zero when:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: |A × B| = |A||B|sin θ.
Step 2: For this to be zero with non-zero vectors: sin θ = 0.
Step 3: θ = 0° or 180°, meaning vectors are parallel (or anti-parallel).
Step 4: Perpendicular vectors give maximum cross product magnitude.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A particle has velocity v = (4t i + 3t² j) m/s. The acceleration at t = 2 s is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: a = dv/dt = d(4t)/dt i + d(3t²)/dt j = 4 i + 6t j.
Step 2: At t = 2 s: a = 4 i + 6(2) j = 4 i + 12 j.
Step 3: x-component of acceleration is constant (4 m/s²), y-component varies linearly with time.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: For a projectile, the ratio of speed at projection point to speed at maximum height is 2:√3. The angle of projection is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Initial speed = u. At max height, speed = ucos θ (vertical component is zero).
Step 2: Given: u/(ucos θ) = 2/√3.
Step 3: 1/cos θ = 2/√3 → cos θ = √3/2.
Step 4: θ = 30°.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Image-based: The figure shows vector resolution. A vector F of magnitude 10 N makes angle 37° with horizontal. Its horizontal component is:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Horizontal component = F cos θ.
Step 2: = 10 × cos(37°) = 10 × 0.8 = 8 N.
Step 3: Vertical component = 10 × sin(37°) = 10 × 0.6 = 6 N.
Step 4: Check: √(8² + 6²) = √(64 + 36) = √100 = 10 N. ✓
questions.imagePrompt: Vector F shown as arrow at angle 37° above horizontal, horizontal component F_x = Fcos37° drawn as dashed line along x-axis, vertical component F_y = Fsin37° drawn as dashed line along y-axis, right triangle formed with components, labeled magnitudes 10 N, 8 N, 6 N, angle 37° marked, clean force diagram
